strategy.success_criterion: On buggy revision 03c1d566ee26: running the test_enet_alpha_max parametrization with positive=True must fail because ElasticNet(alpha=0.99*alpha_max, fit_intercept=..., positive=True) still produces an all-zero coefficient vector (so the assertion assert_array_less(1e-3, np.max(np.abs(reg.coef_))) fails). On fixed revision for PR#32768: the same assertion should pass (coefficients become nonzero for the slightly smaller alpha).
strategy.numerical_probe: The test does not need an external probe; it relies on these transitions: (1) ElasticNetCV(..., positive=True).alpha_ (alpha_max) yields coefficients exactly/near zero via assert_allclose(reg.coef_, 0, atol=1e-5); (2) ElasticNet(alpha=0.99*alpha_max, positive=True) yields max(abs(coef_)) > 1e-3 via assert_array_less(1e-3, np.max(np.abs(reg.coef_))).

input_output_examples.input: X = [[3.0, -1.0], [2.0, -5.0], [5.0, -3.0], [1.0, -4.0]]; beta = [1, -2]; y = X @ beta; parameters include fit_intercept=False/True (param), positive=True (param), sample_weight either array([1,10,1,10]) or None (param); run ElasticNetCV(alphas=1, cv=2, eps=1, fit_intercept=..., positive=True).fit(X,y,sample_weight=...). Then let alpha_max = reg.alpha_. Fit ElasticNet(alpha=0.99*alpha_max, tol=1e-8, fit_intercept=..., positive=True).fit(X,y, sample_weight=...). Then check: assert_allclose(reg.coef_, 0, atol=1e-5) for alpha_max and assert_array_less(1e-3, max(abs(coef_))) for 0.99*alpha_max.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: For positive=True, the second assertion fails because max(abs(coef_)) remains <= 1e-3 (effectively all-zero coefficients).
input_output_examples.expected_output: For positive=True, the second assertion passes because max(abs(coef_)) > 1e-3 (non-all-zero coefficients).

risks: This bug/failure may be sensitive to the exact BLAS/OpenMP setup because scikit-learn coordinate descent uses OpenMP/libgomp (evidence references scikit_learn.libs/libgomp-a34b3233.so.1.0.0). If your environment uses a different OpenMP runtime or BLAS, the failure might not reproduce identically.
The evidence does not state the exact fixed commit SHA; you must locate the PR#32768 merge commit (or the commit after 03c1d566ee26) and run the same test there to confirm the transition.

Test parametrization covers both dense and sparse (X_is_sparse), fit_intercept True/False, sample_weight None/array([1,10,1,10]). The failure is expected specifically in the positive=True branches, but it may occur for only a subset (e.g., dense vs sparse) depending on the bug’s implementation details.
If you don’t build/install scikit-learn from source at the target commit (and instead use a prebuilt wheel), the bug may not be present or may be masked by a different build configuration.
